archetype.name: Point Guard (play-action timing passer)
archetype.definition: A Shanahan-system distributor who wins by throwing on time and accurately over the middle off play-action, spreading the ball to Evans, Kittle, McCaffrey and Samuel. He adds just enough scrambling to punish coverage that sits back.

report.headline: Elite efficiency built on scheme and accuracy, but the TD rate will cool
report.take:
Purdy is doing what he has done in his best seasons, with more polish. He ranks third among 43 qualifiers in EPA per dropback (0.397) and adjusted net yards per dropback, first in TD rate and first in sack rate. His completion rate over expected (5.98) fits a player who has posted 5+ CPOE in three of his four seasons. That accuracy is the core of who he is, not a hot streak. The engine is familiar: the middle of the field yields 0.826 EPA a throw, and under-center snaps (mostly play-action) carry a 16.2 CPOE against -0.6 from shotgun. The offense lives on timing throws that Shanahan's run looks open up.

The protection story is better than the tracking suggests. His 3.05-second time to throw is long, much like 2025's 3.17. But he's pressured on only 11.3% of dropbacks (4th) and the line ranks 4th in hit rate allowed. When things do break down he scrambles well: 12 scrambles for 121 yards, 7 first downs and 0.692 EPA each. His designed runs (1.5 yards a carry) are dead weight. The legs are a bailout tool, not part of the plan.

The numbers hide how much of the season came against soft defenses. Against Miami and Arizona, now ranked 28th and 29th in defensive EPA, he put up +23.3 and +22.9 passing EPA. Against Denver (7th) and Seattle (2nd) he managed +8.5 and -2.0. All three of his sacks came in Seattle. The red zone is the other flag: 9 TDs on 27 plays with a 21.8 CPOE is not a repeatable rate, and 13 TDs on 142 attempts will drift down. His career interception ranks (55th of 66, 50th of 60, 49th of 63) also say the two picks so far are on the lucky side.

Going forward, the floor is high because the scheme, the line and his accuracy are stable. The ceiling depends on the opponent and the receiving room. Deebo Samuel is out for at least a couple of weeks and Christian Kirk hasn't played, so the target tree narrows to Evans, Kittle and McCaffrey. That concentrates volume but removes a YAC option that kept defenses honest underneath.

strengths.title: Accuracy is a career trait
strengths.body: His CPOE of 5.98 ranks 7th, and he was 5th in both 2023 and 2025. It comes from on-time throws in a scheme that schools open windows, and it holds up across seasons. That makes it the most bankable part of his profile.

strengths.title: Clean pocket, almost no sacks
strengths.body: He's pressured on only 11.3% of dropbacks and leads qualifiers in sack rate. The line ranks 4th in hit rate allowed, and his pressure-to-sack rate has improved for two straight years (0.167 in 2025). Even with a long time to throw, he isn't taking drive-killing sacks.

strengths.title: Middle-of-field and scramble value
strengths.body: Throws over the middle return 0.826 EPA with a 77.8% completion rate, the heart of the Shanahan timing game. When the play breaks down, his scrambles add 0.692 EPA apiece and have moved the chains 7 times in 12 tries. Both come from skill and system, so they should hold.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate will regress
concerns.body: His 9.2% TD rate leads the league, built on 9 red-zone TDs from 27 plays and a 21.8 red-zone CPOE. That is far above what anyone sustains near the goal line, and Evans' 1.006 EPA per target is also running hot. Expect TDs to come down even if the efficiency stays strong.

concerns.title: Good defenses have slowed him
concerns.body: His two big EPA games came against defenses now ranked 28th and 29th. Against Denver and Seattle he was far more ordinary, with bad-throw rates of 24.1% against Denver and -2.0 EPA plus all three sacks in Seattle. This is partly schedule, but it marks the line between very good and dominant.

concerns.title: Receiver depth is thinning
concerns.body: Samuel is out with a hamstring strain after 20 targets on 58% of snaps, and Kirk is unlikely to practice. That leaves Evans, Kittle and McCaffrey to carry the load, with Demarcus Robinson as the next man up on a tiny sample. The issue is short-term, but it narrows what defenses must cover.

trend.note: His passing EPA went +4.8, +23.3, +22.9, +8.5, then -2.0, tracking opponent quality almost exactly. The spikes came against bottom-four defenses and the dip against Seattle's 2nd-ranked unit. The underlying accuracy and protection held steady throughout.

nextGame.headline: Banged-up Washington secondary is a good get-right spot
nextGame.body:
Washington is the soft kind of opponent he feasted on in Weeks 2 and 3, not the Seattle or Denver kind. The Commanders rank 25th in pass-defense EPA and 27th in sack rate, and they allow 23.2 PPR and 3 TDs a game to quarterbacks (31st and 30th). They rank 7th against the run, and offenses pass on them 6.1 points more than expected, the 3rd-strongest pass funnel. That nudges Shanahan toward the air. Tight ends have crushed them, scoring 10.7 PPR over their own averages (worst in the league), which sets up Kittle working the middle where Purdy lives.

Availability tilts it further. Washington's safety room is gutted: Nick Cross (99% of snaps), Percy Butler and Tyler Owens are all out, CB Trey Amos is on IR and edge Charles Omenihu is out. That means a weaker rush and a thin back end against seam and crossing routes. On his side, Samuel's absence costs a YAC option, while Juszczyk could return to help the under-center play-action game. Washington is also missing QB Marcus Mariota (54% of snaps) and WR Stefon Diggs, which could tilt game script toward SF. Wind is forecast around 13 mph with 20 mph gusts, but it's early and below the level that usually hurts passing.

keyMatchups.title: Kittle against a leaky middle
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks last in PPR allowed over average to the top tight end and 25th in EPA per play against TE1s. With Samuel out, Kittle's 28 targets should grow. It is the cleanest path to efficient volume.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted safeties versus play-action
keyMatchups.body: With Cross and two backup safeties out, Washington's 19th-ranked deep defense gets thinner. Purdy's intermediate throws (0.577 EPA) and deep shots (0.564 EPA) should find open space behind play-action.

keyMatchups.title: Run wall pushes the ball to Purdy
keyMatchups.body: Washington is 7th in run-defense EPA and 3rd in explosive runs allowed, and offenses lean pass against it. SF's own run game is only 13th in EPA. Expect a pass-heavier script than usual.

nextGame.watch: How the targets redistribute without Samuel. Kittle and Evans soaking up volume over the middle would mean another 20+ point outing.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect him to stay a top-five efficiency quarterback. The accuracy, the protection and the scheme have carried across his career, and the defense (4th in EPA) keeps game scripts friendly. What will come down is the scoring: a league-leading TD rate built on a red-zone CPOE over 20 normalizes toward roughly two TDs a game. His career interception history suggests a few more picks are coming than his current 1.4% rate implies.

Yardage should hold in the 230-270 range, with spikes against weak secondaries and quieter days against top-ten defenses like the ones in Weeks 4 and 5. Samuel's return around early November and Kirk's possible debut matter for the ceiling. Until then the offense is more concentrated and a bit easier to defend for good units.

bets.reason: Washington allows 287.6 passing yards a game to QBs (28th) and is a strong pass funnel with a 7th-ranked run defense. Its secondary is missing three safeties and CB Amos.
Washington gives up 3 TDs a game to quarterbacks (30th) and is weakest against tight ends. He has thrown at least two TDs in every game this season.
Washington ranks last in PPR allowed over average to TE1s. Samuel's absence frees up targets over the middle, where Purdy produces 0.826 EPA a throw.
SF is 4-1 against the spread with a 4th-ranked defense. Washington's offense is 27th in success rate and is missing Mariota and Diggs.
His rushing comes from scrambles, and Washington's 27th-ranked sack rate and 20th-ranked hit rate mean less pressure to escape. His designed runs average just 1.5 yards against a top-ten run defense.

confidence.note: Five-game sample with soft-opponent spikes, but the core traits match his career.
